Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows collaborators with write access to push to protected branches by merging pull requests. Because MergePullRequest skips branch protection checks and PullRequest.Merge omits hook environment variables, attackers can merge commits into branches restricted to allowlisted users.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to bound the number of records a single GraphQL request may hydrate which allows an authenticated user to exhaust server memory and cause a denial of service via a small query that repeats the runs field under many aliases. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00767

SDDC Manager contains a local privilege-escalation vulnerability.
Affected versions: 9.1.x.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0100); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).

VMware Tools for Windows contains a SAML token signature bypass vulnerability.
Affected versions: 13.x.x.x (fixed in 13.1.5.0); 12.3.x (fixed in 12.5.5).

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.0.11 11.11.7 11.2.10.0 fail to check for a nil result after decoding the HTTP request body which allows an authenticated user to crash the Zoom plugin process, causing denial of service, via sending a JSON null body to the plugin's action endpoints. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00722

A flaw was found in Moodle's Blackboard question import format. Insufficient validation of file paths during the question import process allows an authenticated user with permissions to import questions into a question bank to read arbitrary files accessible to the web server process. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to view sensitive files, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to move other forms' shared assets by supplying their URLs in file upload fields. Attackers can submit a public form with another form's cover or logo URL, causing Storage::move() to relocate it into submissions and break that asset.
In JetBrains Datalore before 2026.4.1 improper authorization allowed notebook viewers to read attached environment variable values
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 improper authorization allowed project administrators to obtain GitLab tokens of other projects
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 privilege escalation from project administrator to system administrator was possible via group merging

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could
allow an authenticated contact user to access information associated with other
clients on the same Automate server through API requests. This may result in
disclosure of information outside the user’s assigned access scope. The issue
is limited to information disclosure and does not extend existing modification
or command execution permissions. This issue is resolved in ConnectWise
Automate 2026.11.

Bolt is a fully open source, adaptable platform for building and running modern websites. Prior to 6.1.4, SQL injection in ListFormatHelper allows authenticated users with upload permission to execute arbitrary SQL queries through /async/select-options and exfiltrate sensitive database contents when general/caching/list_format is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 6.1.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, the authenticated get-unit-log action accepts a caller-controlled logfile value. Validate::string() escapes HTML but leaves path traversal components unchanged. The action joins the caller-controlled logfile to SERVICE_LOGS_DIR without enforcing containment, so traversal can resolve the file read outside that directory. www/controllers/ajax/status/service.php reads and returns the resolved file, and any authenticated user can invoke the action to retrieve files readable by the www-data service account, including application configuration, source code, and the GPG signing-key passphrase. Fixed in 5.13.3.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the apps backup and restore Representational State Transfer (REST) API to prevent subsequent apps backup or restore operations until Splunk Enterprise restarts. This could result in a Denial of Service (DoS).
The vulnerability is possible because the apps backup and restore REST API handlers do not correctly enforce authorization.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user that holds a role with the list_deployment_server capability could access sensitive information from inputs.conf files outside the intended deployment app directory through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not restrict a deployment app name to an existing deployment app before reading input configurations.
For more information see authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.4-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), Deployment server architecture (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/update-your-deployment/9.0/deployment-server-and-forwarder-management/deployment-server-architecture), and inputs.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.16-configuration-file-reference/inputs.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled data in finding exclusion rule metadata. Another authenticated user could later open the Finding Exclusion Rules page. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opened the page. The first user could access data and perform actions available to the later user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape backslashes in finding exclusion rule metadata before adding the values to a page search.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_modinput_identity_manager capability could use Asset and Identity Management to modify protected saved searches and role capabilities. With this access, the user could obtain full administrator access to the Splunk platform.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset and Identity Management does not validate the app namespace before sending a Representational State Transfer (REST) API request with a system authentication token.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Add asset and identity data to Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/asset-and-identity-management/add-asset-and-identity-data-to-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the containers:view permission could access automation history for containers outside the label or tenant scope assigned to the user. This could expose action parameters, connector result summaries, and other investigation and response activity.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk SOAR Representational State Transfer (REST) API checks the permission to view containers but does not restrict automation history to containers within the label or tenant scope assigned to the user.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user whose role grants system_settings:view but not assets:view could access asset and application inventory, tenant identifiers, connector run messages, and stored configuration snapshots through the ingestion status Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the ingestion status REST API checks the system_settings:view permission but does not enforce assets:view or tenant restrictions before it returns asset-derived ingestion records.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.3.1/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), and Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.1/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks could cause automation batches for other events to stop running.
The vulnerability occurs because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the server-provided execution context.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a Splunk SOAR user who can edit and run playbooks for a permitted container label could associate action and callback state with a running playbook outside that container label. This could affect playbook automation for containers that the user cannot view.
The vulnerability is possible because the Playbook Automation API accepts a supplied playbook run identifier without verifying that it is bound to the server-provided playbook execution context.
The vulnerability requires a running playbook on a container label that the user cannot view.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who can edit and run a playbook on a permitted label could cause Splunk SOAR to return custom-function status and callback state from another playbook run.
The issue results from insufficient binding between a custom-function-status request and the playbook run that initiates it.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks on a container label could associate a custom-function callback with another playbook run. The callback could modify the state of a container outside the authorized scope for that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the trusted playbook run and container context.

In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, a user who can read splunkd_access.log or the _internal Splunk index could recover the Stream forwarder authentication key and use it to impersonate a trusted Stream forwarder.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk App for Stream sends the authentication key in an internal request URL, and Splunk records that URL in splunkd_access.log.
For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the search jobs Representational State Transfer (REST) API to access indexed events that the srchFilter setting for the role should hide. The same user could also run internal Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and bypass SPL safeguards for risky commands within indexes that the role can search.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape required field values before it includes them in an internally generated search.
For more information, see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/rest-api-reference/9.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions), authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.5-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands).

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could determine whether a username exists through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web and lock out existing user accounts through repeated login attempts.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise returns different login failure responses for locked existing user accounts and nonexistent usernames.

CKAN is an open-source data management system for data hubs and data portals. Prior to 2.10.11 and 2.11.6, the web user registration flow authenticates a newly registered account without first regenerating the session identifier when server-side session storage is configured. An attacker who can set a session cookie in a victim's browser or obtain the victim's current valid session identifier can reuse that identifier after the victim registers, gaining access to the new account. CKAN uses cookie-based sessions by default, and web registration is disabled by default through ckan.auth.create_user_via_web. This issue is fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6, and 2.12.0.

The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library improperly synchronizes authentication credentials set on a shared HTTP client during request execution. When concurrent requests are dispatched for different principals, one principal's credential may be transmitted on an outbound request intended for another principal, which can result in credential exposure and lead to unauthorized actions performed as the affected principal at the Okta Management API.
IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 does not invalidate session after a logout which could allow an authenticated user to impersonate another user on the system.

baserCMS is a website development framework. Prior to 5.3.0, getAuthenticationService permits an Api/Admin session authentication fallback based on the Referer header, although operator accounts have an Admin auth prefix and cannot obtain an Api/Admin JWT. An authenticated operator can therefore access /baser/api/admin/ endpoints whose permission.php entries have auth => true, including /baser/api/admin/baser-core/site_configs/view.json, even when the corresponding administrative functionality is restricted. This can disclose administrator-restricted configuration information. This issue is fixed in 5.3.0.

On Intel-based macOS systems, the Okta Device Access (ODA) component of Okta Verify for macOS configures a LaunchDaemon service whose program path resolves via a symbolic link in /usr/local/bin. In environments where non-standard directory permissions grant local non-root users write access to this path, the symbolic link target can be modified, causing the LaunchDaemon to execute the replacement binary upon service restart.
IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service due to an out-of-bounds heap read.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.
A vulnerability in Synology Mail Server allows remote authenticated attackers to read and write non-sensitive settings, and disable some non-critical functions.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS or 'Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MultimediaViewer.This issue affects MultimediaViewer: from * before 1.39.13, 1.42.7, 1.43.2, 1.44.0.

Cross-Site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in The Wikimedia Foundation Mediawiki - RedirectManager Extension allows Cross Site Request Forgery.

This issue affects Mediawiki - RedirectManager Extension: from * before 1.3.3.

URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect') vulnerability in the HTML5 scrubber in rrrene html_sanitize_ex allows a remote attacker to force visitors of a page to navigate to a site of the attacker's choosing via a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> element in sanitized HTML. HtmlSanitizeEx.html5/1 keeps attacker-supplied <meta> elements in its output. A meta element acts on the whole document rather than on the fragment it was embedded in, so it can also declare document-wide directives such as Content-Security-Policy.

This is not cross-site scripting. Browsers do not navigate a meta refresh to a javascript: URL, so the uppercase JAVASCRIPT: filter bypass yields no script execution and none was demonstrated.

This issue affects html_sanitize_ex: from 0.3.1 before 1.4.5 and from 1.5.0-rc.0 before 1.5.3.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.11, PyEnvCfg.write() writes prompt values verbatim to the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg format while PyEnvCfg._read_values() parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who influences --prompt, VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, or configuration input can insert a recognized line boundary and additional keys, including home, causing consumers to use an attacker-selected base interpreter or corrupted environment metadata. The security impact requires prompt input from outside the operator's trust boundary; directly supplied prompt content primarily corrupts the operator's own environment. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.11.

A flaw was found in sssd. A local attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a specially crafted Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) request when passkey authentication is enabled. Due to a missing state validation check in passkey Kerberos handling, the PAM responder dereferences an uninitialized pointer and crashes. This failure disrupts authentication services on the host.

In gnss, there is a possible out of bounds write due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to local denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is needed for exploitation. Patch ID: ALPS11309816; Issue ID: MSV-10731.

IBM MQ 9.2.0.0 through 9.2.0.44 LTS, 9.3.0.0 through 9.3.0.42 LTS, 9.4.0.0 through 9.4.0.26 LTS, 9.4.0.0 through 9.4.5.1 CD, and 10.0.0.0 through 10.0.0.5 LTS and CD stores potentially sensitive information in log files that could be read by a local user.
IBM API Connect 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to access internal resources and cause a denial of service due to server-side request forgery.

IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain an access token for another user due to improper authentication. The sign-in flow does not sufficiently verify the identity of the user completing it, which could allow another user's identity to be assumed.

IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to probe internal network resources due to insufficient validation of webhook destination URLs. User-configured webhook addresses are not sufficiently restricted, so the server could be made to contact internal systems.

Improper access control in Progress WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 could allow an authenticated user with certain folder-management permissions to bypass access restrictions and access or modify files belonging to other users.
Missing authentication for critical function in Windows DHCP Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.
Out-of-bounds write in Windows PCI Bus Driver allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.
Use after free in Windows PCI Bus Driver allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.

Grafana's Prometheus data source passes the resource path supplied by the caller to the configured Prometheus server without restricting it to the supported API endpoints [missing path allowlist]. A user with permission to query the data source can read responses from other endpoints on that server using the data source's credentials.

Dell PowerScale InsightIQ, versions 6.3.0 through 6.4.0, containsan Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information disclosure.

Dell PowerScale InsightIQ, versions 6.3.0 through 6.4.0, containsan Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information disclosure.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[additional_previews][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.6.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wpdm_sanitize_array() function strips HTML tags via wp_kses but leaves bare single quotes intact and calls stripslashes_deep() which defeats WordPress magic quotes protection, allowing a single-quote-based attribute breakout payload to be stored verbatim and later rendered without escaping.

The Passster – Password Protect Pages and Content plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (metakeyinput=passster_id | passster_headline)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.21 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can break out of the shortcode attribute context by embedding a ] character in the passster_id or passster_headline meta value to prematurely close the opening shortcode tag, then append a [/passster] closing tag so that the trailing HTML payload is emitted verbatim by do_shortcode() — bypassing the per-attribute escaping present inside render_shortcode() — and the script will also execute in an editor's or administrator's browser when they preview the Contributor's pending post, since filter_the_content() has no edit-permission capability gate.

The WPZOOM Addons for Elementor – Starter Templates & Widgets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'actions[save_builder][data][elements][...][settings][regions][i][link][url] / [pins][i][link][url]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in oauth-token.service.ts that treats PKCE as a substitute for confidential client authentication, skipping client secret verification when omitted. Attackers holding a captured authorization code and PKCE verifier can mint access tokens and 60-day refresh tokens for a confidential client without knowing its secret.

n8n before 2.43.5, 2.44.x before 2.44.1, and 3.x before 3.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Vector Store (OracleDB) node, which does not validate Metadata Filter keys used in vector search queries. Attackers can supply crafted filter keys through untrusted workflow input such as webhooks to read data accessible to the configured Oracle credential.

Wasmtime's wasmtime-wasi crate 48.0.0 before 48.0.8, 49.0.0 before 49.0.5, and 50.0.0 before 50.0.1 contains a time-of-check/time-of-use race in the wasip3 wasi:sockets udp-socket host implementation that lets guests bypass socket_addr_check send restrictions. A malicious guest can race udp-socket.send against udp-socket.connect to deliver attacker-controlled datagrams to addresses the policy permits only for receiving.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_invoice.php, which escapes billing codes for HTML attributes but not for JavaScript strings in an inline onkeyup handler. Clinicians with encounter coding access can save crafted billing codes through diagnosis.php that execute script when a Back Office user enters a payment, exposing patient and financial data or performing actions as that user.

Huginn from 2026.09.09 before 2026.11.09 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability because OutboundProxy.configure! applies the egress proxy only to Faraday and Typhoeus. Authenticated users can configure JiraAgent or WeiboPublishAgent to send HTTParty, open-uri or Net::HTTP requests directly to internal services, with JiraAgent returning response data as events.

Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to take over other users' collections by supplying an updateId to the createOrUpdateCollection GraphQL mutation. Attackers who know a collection id can trigger ownership reassignment without checks, read its items, rewrite metadata, and evict the original owner and collaborators.

FrankenPHP from 1.5.0 before 1.13.0 contains an incomplete environment sandbox vulnerability in which putenv writes to the process-wide OS environment via os.Setenv, leaking values across concurrent requests. Attackers reaching a request path that spawns child processes with the default environment through proc_open or exec can read secrets such as database passwords set by other requests.

Post to Google My Business plugin for WordPress before 3.5.7 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users with Contributor-level privileges or higher to make the server send requests to arbitrary hosts by supplying an unvalidated mbp_post_attachment URL that reaches a raw getimagesize() call in validate_external_image_size() via the preview REST route. Attackers can exploit this to perform internal port scanning, probe internal-only services and cloud metadata endpoints, and trigger GET-based side effects on internal systems, bypassing network perimeter controls since the request originates from the web server.

A flaw was found in dbus when configured with the nonce-tcp transport. An unauthenticated attacker able to connect to an exposed listener can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by opening a connection and withholding the expected authentication token. Because the server processes this verification without enforcing a timeout, the stalled connection blocks the accept process and prevents legitimate clients from establishing new connections.

The Flatsome theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data-text-sec', 'data-title', and 'title' Attributes via Custom HTML Block in all versions up to, and including, 3.20.12 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives server-side sanitization because wp_kses_post permits data-* attributes globally via _wp_add_global_attributes, allowing attacker-controlled values in data-text-sec, data-title, and title attributes to persist in saved post content and be later interpreted as HTML by the ux-countdown, scroll-to, and lightbox-gallery JavaScript behaviors.

Silverstripe Framework is a PHP framework which powers the Silverstripe CMS. Prior to 6.2.13, the HTML sanitiser does not normalize certain control bytes that browsers ignore when parsing URLs. A CMS author can place those bytes before a javascript: URL in stored content so the sanitiser misses the dangerous scheme, and JavaScript executes in the browser of another user who views the content. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.13.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to run code in protected pipelines through a scheduled pipeline execution policy after the policy had been unassigned due to incorrect authorization checks.

The All in One SEO – AI SEO Plugin to Boost SEO Rankings & Traffic (Schema, Local SEO, Sitemap & SEO Insights) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has placed the AIOSEO breadcrumb on the author template, that the site is running WordPress 6.6 or later with the core Interactivity runtime loaded (e.g., via a block theme or core/navigation block), and that a victim clicks the rendered breadcrumb link on the author archive page.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in the network policy hot-reload component where a local attacker with low privileges could bypass updated network policy restrictions through existing L7-inspected tunnels that continue to use the previous policy after a reload. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in L7 policy enforcement for HTTP CONNECT tunnels where a local attacker with low privileges could cause a protection mechanism failure by using nonstandard HTTP methods to bypass policy restrictions. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure and data tampering.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its gateway-to-sandbox transport where a network attacker positioned on the internal path could intercept credentials and tamper with commands and data because the transport accepts any host key without verification, permitting a machine-in-the-middle to impersonate the sandbox endpoint. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and code execution.

NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its layer-7 REST proxy where a sandboxed actor could bypass the proxy's policy enforcement by sending a request whose body framing is interpreted differently by the proxy and the upstream server, allowing a second request to be smuggled past policy checks. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to data tampering and information disclosure.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Shahidul Islam Sky Addons for Elementor sky-elementor-addons allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects Sky Addons for Elementor: from n/a through 4.2.0.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'details[].icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.11 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload bypasses wp_kses_post on save because Gutenberg serializes block attribute JSON with JSON_HEX_QUOT, encoding double-quotes as \u0022 so no raw quote or angle bracket appears in post_content; parse_blocks() restores the literal quote at render time, producing the HTML attribute breakout.

The WP Delicious – Recipe Plugin for Food Bloggers (formerly Delicious Recipes) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'recipeTitle' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.10.10 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core's block-attribute kses pass strips HTML tags but preserves bare double-quote characters, allowing a payload such as x" onerror="alert(1) to survive both the save pipeline and the render-time strip_tags() call, breaking out of the alt attribute of the rendered img element.

The Flying Images: Optimize and Lazy Load Images for Faster Page Speed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.16 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although wp_kses_post sanitizes post content on save, the payload is kses-legal at save time; the plugin's output-buffer rewrite transforms it into an executable form at render time by overwriting the valueless data-src attribute with the unescaped src value, meaning save-time sanitization provides no effective mitigation.

The Image Source Control Lite – Show Image Credits and Captions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'meta[isc_image_licence]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.14.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The licence display feature must be enabled in the plugin settings (enable_licences option), which is a standard configuration for sites using the licence-attribution functionality.

The Delivery & Pickup Date Time for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.3.90. This is due to a nonce-only settings AJAX handler that stores an attribute-breaking value and an administrator settings template that outputs it without HTML attribute escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content/excerpt (REST wp/v2/posts) → stored in post_content/post_excerpt' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor's entity-encoded payload survives save-time wp_kses filtering verbatim and is only decoded into raw script tags at render time via html_entity_decode(), meaning the injected script executes for every visitor — including authenticated Administrators — once an Editor publishes the post through the standard Contributor workflow.

The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 via the `draft_post()` function. This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

The (Simply) Guest Author Name plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the user Biographical Info (description) field in versions up to, and including, 4.42. The plugin unconditionally calls remove_filter('pre_user_description', 'wp_filter_kses') at plugin load (sfly-guest-author.php:17), which strips WordPress core's sanitization of the user description field for users who lack the unfiltered_html capability (Subscribers, Contributors, Authors). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in their own profile Biographical Info that will execute whenever a user accesses a page rendering that author's description (such as an author archive or a single-post author bio in default WordPress themes like Twenty Seventeen and Twenty Fifteen).

The WP Coder – Insert & Manage Code Snippets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'alt_text (WP media REST) → _wp_attachment_image_alt post meta' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an admin-authored image-type snippet exists on the site, as the attacker uploads an image via the standard WordPress media REST endpoint, sets its Alt Text to a double-quote-based payload that survives WordPress core's sanitize_text_field(), and then publishes a post embedding the shortcode.

The Orbit Fox: Duplicate Page, Menu Icons, SVG Support, Cookie Notice, Custom Fonts & More plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title (post_title)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is further enabled by wptexturize deliberately skipping texturization of content inside <code> elements and the default WordPress kses allow-list preserving <code> tags and raw double quotes on save, allowing a crafted title attribute breakout payload to survive storage and the the_title filter chain intact.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 via the 'site_url' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to make web requests to arbitrary locations originating from the web application and can be used to query and modify information from internal services. The Guzzle HTTP client is instantiated with TLS certificate verification disabled and redirect following enabled by default, allowing redirect-based SSRF bypasses and enabling internal port scanning via distinguishable server responses.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

The Jeg Kit for Elementor – Powerful Addons for Elementor, Widgets & Templates for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires a published page containing both a Post Author widget in user_bio mode (rendering the attacker's biography) and any legitimate jkit_client_logo widget, so that client-logo.js is enqueued and the loadCarousel handler fires against the forged widget markup from the bio field.

The JobBoardWP – Job Board Listings and Submissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'job_description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's default public submission workflow auto-provisions a jb_employer account for any visitor, meaning the effective entry point is unauthenticated — the custom role requirement imposes no real barrier on a stock install.

The Widget Manager Light plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'posts' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.18 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. On a default install, any unauthenticated visitor can self-register as a Masteriyo Student through the plugin's public /account/signup/ form without administrator approval, granting them the publish_course_reviews capability required to submit reviews and exploit this vulnerability.
Tanium addressed an improper signature validation vulnerability.
Tanium addressed an improper access controls vulnerability.

The ITRO Popup Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_html' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable by low-privileged roles such as Subscriber when an administrator has explicitly granted that role access to the plugin settings page via the plugin's role selection option.

BizPrint (print-google-cloud-print-gcp-woocommerce) before 4.10.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in its Debug\Core component that allows any authenticated user, including the lowest-privilege Subscriber role, to invoke the getPrinters and sendPrintRequest AJAX actions without a nonce or capability check. Attackers can send a crafted admin-ajax.php request with an arbitrary WooCommerce order_id to dispatch print jobs for other customers' orders and disclose printer configuration, exposing cross-customer PII and abusing printer resources.

Network-AI from 5.11.0 before 5.17.2 contains a CORS misconfiguration in McpStreamableServer that reflects localhost Origins into Access-Control-Allow-Origin regardless of bind interface. Attackers controlling a localhost-origin page or DNS-rebinding name can read unauthenticated /tools and /health responses, exposing tool catalogs and bridge metadata on non-loopback binds.

Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 2.0.3, public/main/course_description/course_description_controller.php assigns contentDescription directly from a teacher's request in the Doctrine-based add and edit paths without cross-site scripting sanitization. The stored value is rendered by src/CoreBundle/Resources/views/Course/about.html.twig through description with raw output, and the /course/{id}/about route is publicly accessible. A teacher can store active content that executes when an authenticated or unauthenticated visitor views the course description, enabling session theft, credential phishing, defacement, or actions in an authenticated victim's session. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.
IBM Financial Transaction Manager (FTM) 3.2.13.0 through 3.2.13.0 Interim Fix 006 stores potentially sensitive information in environment variables that could be read by a local user.

A vulnerability was identified in Relaticle up to 3.10.0. This affects the function mapToField of the file packages/ImportWizard/src/Livewire/Steps/MappingStep.php of the component Import Wizard. Such manipulation of the argument Target leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.0, failed Railpack builds and database backups propagate an execution error containing the full command, exposing application environment variables, database passwords, and S3 access keys embedded in those commands. When the corresponding App Build Error or Database Backup notification setting is enabled, the disclosure can send secrets to email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, or webhooks; the same secrets are written separately to persistent Dokploy container logs, which may be accessible to more principals than the affected service. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

Executing a manipulation can lead to improper input validation. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been published and may be used. The built-in regular expression name finder for latitude and longitude coordinates uses a pattern that is vulnerable to excessive backtracking. An attacker who can supply text that an application analyzes with this name finder can cause high CPU consumption, leading to denial of service. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.5.13 or 3.0.0, which fix the issue.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 credential leakage via Mercurial subrepository URLs was possible

The Slimbox Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'el.title (HTML-decoded title attribute of a stored <a rel^=lightbox> element)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a companion plugin such as bbPress that permits low-privileged users to store anchor elements with arbitrary title and rel attributes, as WordPress core comment handling does not preserve rel on anchor tags by default.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1 stored XSS on the Changes page was possible

The Foxtool All-in-One: Contact chat button, Custom login, Media optimize images plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'foxtool_image_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A subscriber-level attacker can store a payload in their own profile's foxtoolpic user-meta that executes in an administrator's browser session when the administrator views the user via the Users → Edit screen.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2 stored XSS in external change viewer links was possible

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Wi-Fi Configuration Server Missing Authentication Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to modify Wi-Fi configuration on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of Wi-Fi configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29068.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a dashboard that contains attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL). The SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opens the dashboard. With this access, the user who created the dashboard could expose stored credentials and write data to an index.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape field names in searches that use the rename command.
For more information see rename (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/spl-search-reference/10.4/search-commands/rename) and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could inject a malicious script into the name of a private saved search. If another user subsequently enables, disables, or edits the corresponding platform alert in the Monitoring Console, the injected script executes within that user's browser session, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to view sensitive information or modify data in Splunk Enterprise.
The vulnerability is possible because the Monitoring Console does not safely handle saved-search names in the platform alert workflow.
For more information see Enable and configure platform alerts (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/monitor/10.4/configure-the-monitoring-console/enable-and-configure-platform-alerts) and About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, and 10.0.12, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could overwrite shared application dashboard views with arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands. When another authenticated user opens an affected dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise executes the injected SPL using the viewing user's permissions, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to access or modify data available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected app grants the "power" Splunk role write access to shared dashboard views that should be writable only by the "admin" Splunk role.
The vulnerability is possible because the Splunk App for Splunk Observability Cloud grants the "power" Splunk role write access to shared dashboard views that should be writable only by the "admin" Splunk role

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Intrusion Detection data. If another user who can access the Intrusion Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Intrusion Search dashboard encodes data-model field values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Network dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/network-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Network Resolution data. If another user who can access the Domain Name System Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify some data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Domain Name System Search dashboard encodes data-model field values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Protocol intelligence dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/protocol-intelligence-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in vulnerability scan data. If another user who can access the Vulnerability Scan Details dashboard selects an affected value, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the value. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the affected value.
The vulnerability is possible because the Vulnerability Scan Details dashboard does not validate destination values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Vulnerability Scan Details (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/vulnerability-scan-details) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled certificate values. If another user who can access the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard encodes certificate values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Protocol intelligence dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/protocol-intelligence-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to send the stored root credential for an external credential store to a host that the user controls. Depending on the configuration, the exposed credential could include an access token, application secret, account password, or client certificate.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR reuses the stored credential when the user changes the external credential store endpoint without supplying replacement credentials.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings view and edit permissions could test a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol authentication provider and cause Splunk SOAR to send a stored directory service account bind password to a host that the user controls.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR reuses a stored directory service provider credential when an authentication test uses a different directory service connection destination.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with permission to edit playbooks and repositories could store a modified utility block in a playbook. If a user that holds a role with permission to edit playbook code later opens and saves the playbook in the Visual Playbook Editor, a subsequent playbook run could send a Representational State Transfer (REST) API delete request to a resource outside the intended data list. The user account that runs the playbook must have permission to delete the target resource.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not prevent a utility block from changing the intended REST API request path.
For more information see Data management automation API (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/python-playbook-api-reference/6.3.0/automation-api/data-management-automation-api) and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.
IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive credentials due to the use of a hard-coded cryptographic key.

Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the MCP run_recipe tool in src/core/mcp_handler.py accepts a caller-controlled recipe_name that load_recipe() in src/cli/recipe.py appends to the src/recipes path without resolved-path containment. Parent-directory segments can therefore make Flyto load and execute a YAML workflow outside the bundled recipe directory, bypassing the boundary represented by list_recipes(). This does not necessarily provide unrestricted code execution because available workflow modules remain subject to Flyto's module policy, but it permits unintended execution of allowed browser, network, file, and data-processing modules. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. An attacker with a connection to the X11 server, either locally or remotely, can exploit this without user interaction. This could lead to the disclosure of memory contents or cause a denial of service by crashing the server.

An attacker with access to the X11 server can exploit this by sending a malformed request, which causes the server to read beyond its intended memory boundaries. This can lead to the exposure of sensitive information or cause the server to crash, resulting in a denial of service.
