In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_byteorder: remove multi-register support

64bit byteorder conversion is broken when several registers need to be
converted because the source register array advances in steps for 4 bytes
instead of 8:

  for (i = ...
      src64 = nft_reg_load64(&src[i]);
                             ~~~~~ u32 *src
      nft_reg_store64(&dst64[i],

Remove the multi-register support, it has other issues as well:

Pablo points out that commit
caf3ef7468f7 ("netfilter: nf_tables: prevent OOB access in nft_byteorder_eval")
alters semantics: before the loop operated on registers, i.e.
 for ( ... )
   dst32[i] = htons((u16)src32[i])

 .. but after the patch it will operate on bytes, which makes this
 useless to convert e.g. concatenations, which store each compound
 in its own register.

Multi-convert of u32 has one theoretical application:

ct mark . meta mark . tcp dport @intervalset

Because ct mark and meta mark are host byte order, use with
intervals has to convert the byteorder for ct/meta mark value
to network byte order (bigendian).

nftables emits this:
 [ meta load mark => reg 1 ]
 [ byteorder reg 1 = hton(reg 1, 4, 4) ]
 [ ct load mark => reg 9 ]
 [ byteorder reg 9 = hton(reg 9, 4, 4) ]
 ...

I.e. two separate calls.  Theoretically it could be changed to do:
 [ meta load mark => reg 1 ]
 [ ct load mark => reg 9 ]
 [ byteorder reg 1 = htonl(reg 1, 4, 8) ]
 ...

But then all it would take to change the set to
meta mark . tcp dport . ct mark

... and we'd be back to two "byteorder" calls. IOW, support to
convert a range of registers is both dysfunctional and dubious.

Simplify this: remove the feature.

Pablo Neira Ayuso points out that nftables before 1.1.0 can generate
incorrect byteorder conversions, see 9fe58952c45a,
"evaluate: skip byteorder conversion for selector smaller than 2 bytes"
in nftables.git).  Affected rulesets fail to load with this change and
old userspace due to 'len != size' check.

Local privilege escalation vulnerability in Iperius Backup 8.8.3, due to insufficient separation between the graphical user interface running with elevated privileges and local users with low privileges. When the backup service is configured to run persistently with Administrator privileges, a local attacker with low privileges can use the native Windows dialogues exposed by the application to run programmes that inherit its elevated context. This allows commands to be executed with SYSTEM or Administrator privileges, depending on the application’s context, and compromises the affected Windows system.

repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When event_notification_command is configured, repmgr substitutes the %a (node name), %c (connection string) and %d (details) placeholders into the command and runs it through the shell. %a and %c are inserted without escaping, and %d escapes only double quotes, so shell command substitution still works inside the quoting the documentation recommends. The node name and connection string come from node records in the repmgr.nodes table. An attacker with the credentials of a non-superuser repmgr database user can write a crafted node record and run OS commands, as the operating system user that runs repmgr or repmgrd (usually postgres), on other cluster nodes that process an event using these placeholders. The %a placeholder of failover_validation_command has the same flaw. Deployments whose repmgr database user is a superuser gain no new capability, because a superuser can already run OS commands, and deployments that do not use these placeholders are not affected. The issue is fixed in repmgr 5.5.1. After upgrading, operators must remove any quotes they placed around these placeholders, because a placeholder left inside double quotes is still open to command injection.

Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in custom invoice payment terms. An authenticated Manager can save a crafted custom payment-term value. When an authorized user opens Invoice Settings for the same company, Akaunting inserts the stored value into a client-side event-handler expression, causing attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the victim's authenticated origin.
A hard-coded root password in Microchip TimePictra platform installation files could allow an attacker with access to those files to obtain privileged credentials

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Microchip the TimePictra platform could allow an authenticated, low-privileged attacker to store malicious script content that executes when another user views the affected page

Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability through invoice import. An authenticated user with invoice-creation permission can import HTML in an invoice status field. When another authenticated user opens that invoice's edit form, Akaunting renders the stored status in a hidden input with raw Blade output, allowing attacker-controlled markup to execute in the victim's Akaunting origin.

The vulnerability lies in the way application credentials are handled within the BOSH deployment.
bosh-openstack-cpi-release: all versions from v55 to v55.0.4 (inclusive)
A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Qt Framework QDomDocument::setContent() XML parsing path of the Qt XML module (qtbase).

A vulnerability in the administration REST interface of Azul Payara allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass secure-admin remote-access restrictions by supplying an arbitrary value in the X-GlassFish-authToken HTTP header. The header's presence waives the remote-rejection check before the token is validated, and an invalid token falls through to password-based authentication, which succeeds without credentials on default domains configured with an empty administrative password. Successful exploitation grants execution of arbitrary administrative commands, equivalent to complete compromise of the server.

Blind SQL injection vulnerability in the public endpoint `public/webhook/receiver.php` of the WhatsApp module for Dolibarr 1.9. The phone number value derived from the `data.key.remoteJid` parameter, received via a JSON request, is incorporated into an SQL query without escaping or parameterization. With the WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_ALLOW option enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker could manipulate this parameter to alter the query. Exploitation using a timing-based technique could allow an attacker to extract information from the database and cause service disruption.

Improper neutralization of CRLF sequences ('CRLF injection') vulnerability in ibi WebFOCUS.

This issue affects WebFOCUS: 9.1, from 9.2 through 7, and from 9.3 through 7.

Improper verification of the source of a communication channel vulnerability in Opera Neon on macOS and Windows allows a malicious browser extension to take control of the browser by sending commands through MCP Hub to the built-in Browser Operator extension. This issue affects Opera Neon MCP Hub extension: 0.0.1.

Authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in TIBCO TIBCO Platform’s Self-Hosted Control Plane.

This issue affects TIBCO Platform’s Self-Hosted Control Plane: from 1 through 1.21.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, insufficient validation of custom claims on OIDC accounts allowed a user with permission to edit accounts to cause Octopus Server to issue signed OIDC tokens that impersonate a different project. This could grant access to external systems, such as cloud providers or other Octopus instances, that trust that project's identity.
An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication controls to access restricted resources on the Citrix NetScaler Console appliance

In affected versions of Octopus Server, incorrect validation of the external identity linked to a newly registered user could result in that user receiving the LDAP-mapped team memberships and associated permissions of another user. This issue only affects instances with LDAP authentication enabled and LDAP groups mapped to Octopus teams.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, incorrect validation of changes a user made to their own LDAP identity allowed them to edit that identity even when an Administrator had disabled self-service identity editing. This could result in the user gaining membership of teams mapped to external LDAP groups they do not belong to, and potentially escalating to full administrative privileges if any of those teams are privileged.
An uncontrolled recursion vulnerability has been discovered in the Qt QXmlSimpleReader XML parsing functionality of the Qt 5 Core Compatibility APIs module (Qt 6) and the Qt XML module (Qt 5).

Docker Sandboxes reuses existing state and configuration directories without verifying their ownership. If sbx or sandboxd is run as root with HOME or, on Linux, XDG_STATE_HOME pointing to an attacker-controlled location, a local unprivileged user can substitute control-plane sockets and configuration trusted by the root process, potentially executing commands as root. Exploitation requires a privileged invocation with an attacker-influenced environment. The issue affects Linux and macOS and is fixed in version 0.53.0.

Docker Sandboxes can silently republish a sandbox service after an operator removes its automatically assigned host-port mapping. The daemon removes the active binding but retains the original publication request, allowing a later port change or sandbox restart to publish the service again on a new host port. An attacker able to reach the restored endpoint may regain access to the service. Both TCP and UDP mappings are affected. Exposure is limited to the original bind address, which defaults to loopback. The issue is fixed in version 0.53.0.

A user with query access to a Google Cloud Monitoring data source can use its resource proxy to send requests to other Cloud Monitoring API paths with the data source's credentials, and read data from any project those credentials can reach. When the data source forwards the user's OAuth identity or uses Workload Identity Federation, the impact depends on that credential's permissions. Fixed in Google Cloud Monitoring plugin 12.6.7.

Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the XLSX invoice-import workflow. An authenticated Manager can import a child invoice whose invoice number contains HTML and is linked to a recurring invoice. When a victim opens that recurring invoice, Akaunting raw-renders the stored child number in an anchor, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute in the victim's browser.

In FRRouting, bgpd does not correctly close a BGP session when the Send Hold Timer (RFC 9687) expires, i.e. when a neighbor has stopped accepting data from the router for twice the hold time. The connection is closed, but bgpd still considers the session to be up. A BGP neighbor that keeps sending KEEPALIVEs but stops reading from its connection, at a time when the router has a large amount of data to send to it (for example while sending it a full routing table), can trigger this. If the neighbor announced Graceful Restart support, bgpd crashes shortly after the session is closed, taking down all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat this each time bgpd restarts. Otherwise, the session stays stuck in the Established state: the neighbor's routes stay installed and keep being advertised to other peers, and the neighbor cannot reconnect until an operator clears the session manually. The neighbor does not need to be malicious; an overloaded or stuck peer can trigger the same behavior. No special configuration is required: any established BGP neighbor can trigger the issue, and Graceful Restart helper mode, which leads to the crash, is enabled by default.

The Symfony FrameworkBundle framework.trusted_proxies option and the HttpFoundation Request::setTrustedProxies() method trust remote clients as reverse proxies when the private_ranges shortcut is used, allowing remote attackers to spoof the client IP address, host and scheme in Symfony FrameworkBundle versions 7.1 prior to 7.4.23 and 8.x prior to 8.1.11, and HttpFoundation versions 7.2 prior to 7.4.23 and 8.x prior to 8.1.11. The private_ranges and PRIVATE_SUBNETS keywords resolved to IpUtils::PRIVATE_SUBNETS, the deny list of NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient, which lists the private and special-purpose prefixes a server must not connect to. Since the fix for CVE-2026-48736 (7.4.13 and 8.0.13), this list also covers the IPv6 prefixes that embed an IPv4 address: IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), IPv4-compatible (::/96), 6to4 (2002::/16), Teredo (2001::/32) and NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96). The IPv4-mapped entry has been in the list since the private_ranges shortcut was introduced, in 7.1 for framework.trusted_proxies and in 7.2 for Request::setTrustedProxies(). Over-blocking is safe for a deny list, but when the same entries are used as the allow list of trusted proxies, they trust remote clients. A client whose connection arrives with such a source address is treated as a reverse proxy, and the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Port and X-Forwarded-Prefix headers it sends are honoured. For example, with Request::setTrustedProxies(['private_ranges'], ...), a request with REMOTE_ADDR set to ::ffff:203.0.113.7 and the headers X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.9, X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example.com and X-Forwarded-Proto: https makes getClientIp() return 10.0.0.9, getHost() return evil.example.com and isSecure() return true. Two kinds of deployments are exposed: a server listening on the IPv6 wildcard address without IPV6_V6ONLY reports every IPv4 client in the IPv4-mapped form, so every client is trusted, and a server reachable over IPv6 trusts any client sourcing from 6to4 or Teredo space, which is globally routed, whatever its listener. A spoofed client address defeats IP allow lists, rate limiting and audit logs; a spoofed host poisons the URLs written into password reset and login link e-mails and into shared caches; a spoofed scheme satisfies requires_channel: https over plain HTTP. Symfony 6.4 does not point any trusted proxy setting at IpUtils::PRIVATE_SUBNETS and is not affected by default, but an application that passes that constant to Request::setTrustedProxies() itself could be exposed in the same way on any version. This issue is fixed in 7.4.23 and 8.1.11.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. Prior to 7.4.5, Astro rendered a string used as a dynamic element name as raw HTML after applying an incomplete character filter. A / in the string could make an HTML parser treat the remainder as attributes, allowing untrusted element-name input to inject event-handler markup. The .astro dynamic-tag renderer, JSX renderer, and MDX renderer were affected, and exploitation required an application to use request-controlled or stored untrusted data as all or part of an element name. This issue is fixed in version 7.4.5.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.7.3 until 9.1.2, the @astrojs/svelte renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. Request-controlled slot names containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Svelte component using a client:* directive and dynamic rendering of the attacker-chosen slot; components that did not render that slot emitted only Astro's escaped fallback content. Both server rendering and client-side hydration used the unsafe slot name. This issue is fixed in version 9.1.2.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 0.2.0 until 7.1.2, the @astrojs/solid-js renderer inserted a named slot into the quoted name attribute of an astro-slot wrapper without HTML escaping. A request-controlled slot name containing a quote could terminate the attribute and inject active HTML. Exploitation required a hydrated Solid component using a client:* directive and dynamic access to the attacker-chosen slot property; a component that did not render that slot emitted only escaped fallback content. This issue is fixed in version 7.1.2.

Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpoint compared the requested local-image path with the build output directory without preserving case on case-sensitive filesystems. A sibling directory whose path differed from the output directory only by letter case could therefore pass the containment check, allowing an unauthenticated requester to read image files accepted by the image service from outside the output directory. Exploitation required on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a preexisting case-variant sibling directory; ordinary traversal to unrelated paths was already rejected. This issue is fixed in Astro version 7.4.7.

Pillow is a Python imaging library. From 1.0 through 12.3.0, ImageFileDirectory_v2.load() in src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py retains a separate bytes object for each out-of-line IFD tag value without limiting the total data read or preventing distinct tags from referencing the same file region. A small crafted TIFF or EXIF-bearing JPEG, PNG, WebP, or MPO can therefore cause memory use quadratic in the input size. TIFF and some JPEG paths trigger parsing during Image.open(), while other formats are exposed when EXIF is requested, including through getexif() or ImageOps.exif_transpose(). The declared pixel dimensions do not bound this metadata allocation, so decompression-bomb checks do not prevent process memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to improper cryptographic signature verification in the JWT refresh logic. An authenticated low-privilege user can submit self-crafted​ ​JWT​ containing​ ​an existing user​ ​identifier and, due to the lack of signature validation,​​  obtain​ ​a ​​valid,​​ fully-signed​​ session ​​token​​ for​​ any ​​account ​​in​ ​the​ ​system. This allows the attacker to impersonate any user, including administrators.
This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Dynamic LINQ injection. Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject conditional expressions into the sort parameter of paginated administrative endpoints. Analyzing the returned result order allows the attacker to extract value of any field character by character, leading to potential exposure of sensitive data.


This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Due to improper input validation, an authenticated attacker can inject malicious scripts into givenName and surname parameters via the /api/auth/profile endpoint. When an administrator visits the admin changelog logs, the injected script is automatically executed, in his browser.


This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored XSS via content parameter in Tiny editor functionality. Authenticated attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JS into website, which will be rendered/executed when user tries to edit changed entry.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS is vulnerable to Stored XSS in avatar upload functionality. Authenticated attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JS into website, which will be rendered/executed when visiting an URL leading to a edited avatar.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS restricts the ability to upload files via the UI to specific file types. However, an avatar upload functionality allows an attacker to upload files of any type and extension without restriction.
This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Edito CMS sends JWT token via GET requests. This allows a local attacker with access to browser history to obtain valid JWT token and perform action on behalf of the victim. The token is valid for only short period of time; after that time, it expires and can no longer be used.



The vendor assessed the likelihood of exploitation as very low and determined that a fix is not necessary.

In the 6.3.x branch, this allows the attacker to trigger HTTP requests under their control (SSRF); in 7.0.3, it allows the attacker to read local files and access internal HTTP resources from the server.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.

Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files by injecting traversal sequences via the x-zipline-file-extension header. Attackers can upload a file with a poisoned stored name and short expiry so LocalDatasource deletion removes chosen files, causing denial of service or data loss.

A buffer overread caused by an integer-overflow in Proc/SProcXResQueryClientIds in X.Org xwayland before 24.1.15 and X Server before 21.1.26 could be used by attackers on authenticated X clients to crash the server or leak out information.

This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API.

 

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. 



The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs.

In FRRouting, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.

P-Net before 1.0.4 routes a received RTA alarm frame to an Application Relationship using only the destination alarm reference in the frame, without checking the source of the frame. A host with ADJACENT network access can abort an established Application Relationship with a single alarm ERROR frame, or deliver forged alarm notifications with chosen type, slot, subslot, USI and payload to the application.

A stack buffer overflow in  ProcXTestFakeInput DeviceValuator handling in X.Org xwayland before 24.1.15 and X server before 21.1.26 could be used by authenticated clients to crash or execute code in the X server.

A integer overflow that can lead to a buffer overrread in the XRes QueryResourceBytes Swap Path in the X.Org xwayland before 24.1.15 and X Server before 21.1.26 on 32bit systems could be used by authenticated clients to crash the X server.

In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_core and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via a compressed Erlang external term in a gRPC message body.

GRPC.Codec.Erlpack.decode/2 (grpc_core/lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex, and lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex before the package split) passes the message body to :erlang.binary_to_term/2. That function inflates a compressed term in full before it returns. The codec sets no limit on the decoded size, and its type checks run only on the decoded term. The server's max_body_size limit counts the compressed bytes of the request. A request with Content-Type: application/grpc+erlpack can therefore make the server allocate a term much larger than the request body.

This issue affects grpc_core: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0; grpc: from 0.4.0 before 1.0.0.

Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall all later calls on a shared HTTP/2 connection via calls that the server refuses while their DATA frames are in flight.

The stream handler grpc_stream_h (grpc_server/src/grpc_stream_h.erl) requests flow from Cowboy only for request data that has arrived. When the server refuses a call early, for example because the body exceeds max_body_size or the method is not implemented, Cowboy drops the DATA frames still in flight for that stream. Their bytes are not returned to the connection flow-control window. After enough refused calls the window is empty. No call on that connection can then send a request body, and each call waits until its deadline. Other connections are not affected.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type.

Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another.

This issue affects grpc: from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, lighting_command_decode in src/bacnet/lighting.c decodes its first field with the bounded apdu_size - apdu_len, but every nested decode in the operation switch is called with the original full apdu_size while the read pointer has been advanced to &apdu[apdu_len]. The leaf decoders bound their reads against the size they are told, so they read up to apdu_len bytes past the end of the caller's buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a malformed but non-empty BACnet WriteProperty request can drive the official server demo into a non-terminating request-processing loop with repeated heap-backed side effects. This results in a remote unauthenticated denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption and a non-terminating request path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to occupy a BEAM scheduler indefinitely via a client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request whose body ends inside a gRPC message.

GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.read_stream/1 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy.ex, and the Cowboy adapter in grpc before the package split) asks for more data whenever the buffer does not hold a complete message. Once the request body has ended, every further read returns an empty chunk, so the buffer never changes and the function retries without end. A single 5-byte length prefix sent with END_STREAM keeps one scheduler busy for as long as the connection stays open, and repeated requests exhaust all schedulers.

This issue affects grpc: from 0.3.1 before 1.0.0; grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match `ROUTE` access rules against the fully decoded request path, while the router routes on the raw, still encoded path. An encoded slash (`%2F`) inside a path value is a segment separator for the access check but part of the value for the router, so a request can match a narrow `ROUTE` rule while the handler returns a different, larger resource.



An authenticated caller whose rules grant READ only on parts of a resource can therefore read the whole resource. In the DPP API, a rule such as `/v1/dpps/*/elements/*`, meant to grant only passport elements, also grants the complete passport whose identifier contains `/elements/`. In the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment, a rule such as `/submodels/*/submodel-elements/*/attachment`, meant to grant only file attachments, also grants the complete element whose stored idShort contains `%2F`.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.4.

Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



On a route where multi-auth falls back from wolf-rbac to another successful authenticator, client-supplied Wolf identity headers can remain in the request. A downstream service that relies on those documented headers may therefore receive an identity that was not established by the successful authenticator.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.8.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



On routes using jwe-decrypt with strict: false and a
forward_header distinct from the token header an unauthenticated
client can supply the value the upstream treats as gateway-decrypted
plaintext. Similar can happen when forward-auth is configured with allow_degradation: true, and the auth service is unavailable.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.18.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An authenticated user who holds any one of a route's required permissions or scopes can reach the protected upstream without the others, including HTTP methods the authorization server denied.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 1.4.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, _payload.json URL generation and the experimental early-404 path use a trailing-slash regular expression whose work grows quadratically with a long run of slash characters. An unauthenticated request can synchronously occupy the Node.js event loop and delay other requests when server-side rendering uses isr, swr, or cache route rules, or when experimental.early404 is enabled. Applications without those route rules and without experimental.early404, fully prerendered applications, and client-only applications are unaffected; the impact is limited to availability. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. From 9.5.0 until 10.0.27 and 11.0.9, authenticated users could access ITIL followups, tasks, or solutions generated from templates without a read-permission check on the parent ticket, problem, or change. Depending on the template configuration, this could reveal information from parent items the user could not otherwise read. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.27 and 11.0.9.

envd provides reproducible development environments for humans and agents. In versions starting with 0.3.38 and before 1.3.6, insufficient containment of host-side requirements-file reads in  install.python_packages(requirements=...)  could allow access to files outside the build context. An attacker able to influence build input could cause file contents interpreted as dependency entries to appear in debug logs or build-step metadata, subject to the envd process’s permissions. Exploitation in version 1.3.5 additionally requires concurrent modification of relevant filesystem paths. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.6.

Laravel is a web application framework. Prior to 12.71.0 and 13.40.0, Laravel's Concurrency::run process driver can treat a forged internal result message in child standard output as framework output. An application route must invoke Concurrency::run, and a task must write attacker-controlled bytes at the start of the child's standard output that form a complete JSON document followed by gzip magic bytes. Under those application-specific conditions, an attacker can forge the internal result message and achieve remote code execution. The affected behavior is not exposed by default and requires application code that routes untrusted input into task output. This issue is fixed in versions 12.71.0 and 13.40.0.

In FRRouting (FRR) 8.3 through 10.5.1, bgp_notify_decapsulate_hard_reset() in bgpd/bgp_packet.c does not validate the length of the data field of a received BGP NOTIFICATION Cease/Hard Reset message (RFC 8538). When the data field is exactly one byte long, the function reads one byte past the end of a heap buffer and the 16-bit length of the encapsulated data underflows to 65535, causing a 65535-byte out-of-bounds heap read followed by an assertion failure. A remote BGP peer that has established a session and negotiated the Graceful Restart capability with the Notification (N) bit can send such a message to crash the bgpd daemon, terminating all BGP sessions (denial of service). This is fixed in 10.0.5, 10.1.5, 10.2.6, 10.3.4, 10.4.3, 10.5.2 and 10.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE implementation accepts AtomicWriteFile(record-access) requests that replace existing records with caller-controlled content. If a client replaces a record with shorter data, the backend can shrink the heap allocation and then continue processing with a trailing-copy length derived from the old layout. During that replace path, the RAMFS backend computes the trailing-copy length from the old file layout, then shrinks the heap allocation, and finally uses the stale length in memmove(). As a result, the source range of that memmove() can extend beyond the end of the reallocated heap buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the BACnet FILE object implementation allows remote WriteProperty(PROP_FILE_SIZE) requests to change the size of a stream-access FILE object without checking whether that FILE is marked Read_Only. When the FILE backend is RAMFS, enlarging the file only performs realloc() and updates the stored size; the newly exposed tail region is not initialized before later reads. As a result, a remote client can enlarge a read-only RAMFS-backed stream-access FILE and then immediately retrieve the newly exposed region with AtomicReadFile(stream-access). Depending on the allocator and build configuration, the returned data may contain sanitizer fill bytes, stale heap contents, or other unintended process memory. Shrinking the file through the same path can also remotely truncate content that was intended to be read-only. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

Hubleys is a dashboard for self-hosted services. Prior to version 0.5.2, any authenticated (non-admin) Hubleys user can upload a file with an arbitrary extension as their dashboard "background image," and the server will later serve that file back with a Content-Type derived straight from the attacker's chosen extension - so uploading an .html file gets it served as text/html. Because the endpoint that serves it returns a manually-constructed response rather than going through SvelteKit's normal page-rendering pipeline, the app's configured Content-Security-Policy never gets attached to it either, so a script embedded in the upload runs unrestricted. This issue has been patched in version 0.5.2.

bit-vec is a compact vector of bits. Prior to version 0.10.0, there is undefined behavior if a user performs deserialize from an untrusted source and unsafe get_unchecked. A user of this library may be impacted by incorrect behavior if they perform deserialize from an untrusted source and run operations on the deserialized BitVec. This issue has been patched in version 0.10.0.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, when the pipelined request queue is full, the pure-Python parser stores the unparsed remainder internally and also returns the same data to its caller. After a handler declines an upgrade request, the caller feeds the remainder back to the parser, causing the buffer to grow with each handled request and dispatching already-handled requests to the application again. The issue affects deployments using AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS or otherwise running without the standard C-extension wheel, and can cause excessive memory use and repeated request processing. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the WebSocket reader continues parsing frames already received after the receive queue pauses the transport, and empty messages are not counted toward the queue size. With permessage-deflate, one read of compressed frames can add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the receive queue. A remote peer can send many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them and cause excessive memory use in a server or client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

Use of default credentials vulnerability in Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra SE, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra G2, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra G2 SE, and Johnson Controls iSTAR Edge G2 allows CAPEC‑560: Use of Default Credentials.

This issue affects iSTAR Ultra: before 2.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra SE: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra G2: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra G2 SE: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Edge G2: before 6.9.2.CU02.

Missing protection mechanism for alternate hardware interface vulnerability in Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra and Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra SE allows CAPEC‑554: Functionality Bypass.

This issue affects iSTAR Ultra: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra SE: before 6.9.2.CU02.

Missing protection mechanism for alternate hardware interface vulnerability in Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra SE, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra G2, Johnson Controls iSTAR Ultra G2 SE, and Johnson Controls iSTAR Edge G2 allows CAPEC‑554: Functionality Bypass.

This issue affects iSTAR Ultra: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra SE: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra G2: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Ultra G2 SE: before 6.9.2.CU02; iSTAR Edge G2: before 6.9.2.CU02.

In FRRouting, bgpd frees the sub-TLV chain of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) while routes stored by bgpd still point to it, if the attribute is received from a neighbor that has "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured. A cache added to speed up attribute interning while processing the prefixes of an UPDATE checks whether an interned attribute set may be reused by comparing the parsed attributes with themselves, so the check always succeeds. Interning the parsed attributes for the Adj-RIB-In removes the Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs from them, and the copy that bgpd then interns for the route reuses the cached attribute set, which still holds the sub-TLVs, without taking a reference on them. When the route is later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, the sub-TLV chain is freed while still in use, and bgpd then reads it, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required, and the attribute does not need to be malformed. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. Neighbors without "soft-reconfiguration inbound" are not affected.

When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

usb: xhci: Fix bounce buffer overflow

High-speed devices with out of spec 1024 byte bulk endpoints exist and
are allowed by USB core, but xhci-hcd always sets packet size to 512.
The exact nature of these devices isn't documented, commit fb5ee84ea72c
("USB: Accept bulk endpoints with 1024-byte maxpacket") only states
that they "don't work with xHCI host controllers", whatever it means.

But somebody (or a malicious device) can try, and then the driver will
allocate a 512 byte bounce buffer for this endpoint and may write up to
1024 bytes into it if particular scatter-gather URBs are used, because
xhci_align_td() obtains packet size from the descriptor. Fix this.

As a side effect, TRBs will be aligned to the packet size chosen by the
driver on all endpoints of all speeds. Alignment serves the xHC, not
device, so this is fine. Only out of spec devices are affected anyway.

Batflat CMS does not sanitize data passed to the /contact endpoint. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a POST request with a crafted message, causing arbitrary PHP code execution with www-data user privileges.


The project is no longer maintained and the issue has not been fixed.

The
vulnerability enables any attacker with admin access to dump credentials of all
accounts stored on the device, which can then be reused for lateral movement or
further compromise. Since
passwords are stored or processed in a recoverable format, this represents a
critical failure in secure credential handling.

On Linux and other Unix-like systems, LibreOffice can send the current document as an email attachment with File > Send > Email Document, which starts the mail client through a script bundled with LibreOffice. The script let the shell interpret the name of the document's file, so a file with a crafted name could run commands when it was sent by email. In fixed versions the script passes the file name and the other details to the mail client as plain arguments.

LibreOffice can import PICT images, which may be embedded in documents. Parts of a crafted image could be left unwritten, so leftover memory became part of the imported image and could be saved with the document. In fixed versions the pixels of a new image start out cleared, so any part the image data does not fill is blank.

A document can carry its own user interface customizations, such as keyboard shortcuts, menus and toolbars, which take effect while the document is open. A command bound in these customizations could run a macro or a script even when the macro security settings did not allow the macros of the document, so a user who pressed a shortcut or chose a menu item in a crafted document could run code without any warning. In fixed versions the customizations of a document are treated like its other macro content, and the macro and script commands in them are only kept when the macros of the document are allowed.

LibreOffice documents in ODF format can contain form controls, such as buttons and text fields, and each control names the component that implements it. The component a control named was created even when it was not a form control, and the settings stored with the control were applied to it, so a crafted document could change the configuration of LibreOffice in a way that led to code being run. In fixed versions a control whose component is not a form control is ignored.

LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. When a value in the compiled form used an older record format, it could be read as a different type from the one the existing value held, which corrupted memory. In fixed versions the existing value is cleared before a value in the older format is read.

LibreOffice Writer can open HTML documents, and an HTML document can bind macros to events of the document as a whole, such as the document being opened or closed. Macros bound to these events were not taken into account by the macro security check, so they could run when the document was opened, whatever the macro security level. In fixed versions these macros follow the macro security settings like any other macro in the document.

LibreOffice documents can contain Basic macro libraries. A library protected by a password is stored in the document in a compiled form, which may be read when the document is loaded. An out-of-bounds write existed when the compiled form was read, because the positions of its strings were not checked against the size of the data they refer to, and a type found by name was not checked to be of the right kind. In fixed versions these positions are checked, a library that fails the check is not loaded, and a type of the wrong kind is ignored.

LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.

LibreOffice bundles the HSQLDB database engine, which can be used through the generic JDBC database driver as well as through the support for embedded databases. HSQLDB lets SQL statements call Java methods, limited to the classes that are permitted. When HSQLDB was used through the generic JDBC driver this limit did not apply, so SQL in a crafted document could call any Java method and run code. In fixed versions SQL can call only the built-in functions of HSQLDB, whichever way the database is reached.

LibreOffice Calc can link a cell range to an external data source, and the link is saved in the document. A Java database driver for such a link is loaded from a class path. Opening a crafted document could still load a Java database driver from a location outside the local machine and run its code, by a route that the fix for CVE-2026-63277 did not cover. In fixed versions an entry in a Java class path has to be a file URL that names a file on the local machine.

LibreOffice can embed audio and video in documents. Where it plays media with GStreamer, as on Linux, the media is opened when the document is loaded, and a preview image of a video is shown in the document and in its exports, such as PDF. A crafted media file could make GStreamer read a local file and draw its text into the preview image, so that the content of the file ended up in an exported document. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63269. In fixed versions GStreamer opens only media in a short list of common, self-contained container formats.

libvisio is a library that reads drawings in the VSD and VSDX formats. LibreOffice and other applications use it to import such drawings. An out-of-bounds write existed when a crafted VSDX file contained a malformed path from one part of the drawing to another. In fixed versions a malformed path is handled without writing outside its data.

LibreOffice can open a web query file (.iqy), which names a web page to import into a spreadsheet, when the file is given on its command line, for example when a file manager or another program opens the file with LibreOffice. The address in such a file was used without the checks that apply to an address given on the command line directly, so a crafted file could make LibreOffice do something other than open a web page, up to running code. In fixed versions only an http or https address is taken from a web query file.

LibreOffice supports fonts embedded in documents. When a document is exported to PDF, the fonts it uses are embedded in the PDF, and a font in CFF (Compact Font Format) is converted to another font format on the way. An out-of-bounds write existed when the charstring program of a crafted font was interpreted, because some indexes and ranges taken from the font were not checked against the size of the data they refer to. In fixed versions these indexes and ranges are checked, and a font that fails the checks is not converted.

LibreOffice can export documents to PDF protected by a password. With the PDF 2.0 option the file is encrypted with 256-bit AES, using a file encryption key and salts that are meant to be random. The key and the salts were drawn from a pseudo-random number generator that is not suitable for cryptography, so the encryption key of an exported PDF could be recovered without knowing the password. In fixed versions the key and the salts are drawn from the random source of the operating system.

LibreOffice has an option, called stealth mode in earlier advisories, that stops documents from outside the trusted file locations from loading linked images and other content. The option is not on by default. With the option on, a linked background image in an HTML document was still fetched while the document was imported. In fixed versions a linked background image is checked against the option like other linked images, and is not fetched when the option blocks it.

LibreOffice can import EMF, EMF+ and WMF images, which may be embedded in documents. Several out-of-bounds reads existed in the readers for these formats, because sizes, counts and offsets taken from a crafted image were not checked against the data the image actually holds. In fixed versions these values are checked against the size of each record and the data that remains, and a record that fails the checks is not used.

: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information vulnerability in Johnson Controls Open Blue Companion Android App on Android allows : Retrieve Embedded Secrets from Software.

This issue affects Open Blue Companion Android App: before R2.22.0.

LibreOffice can open PDF files in Draw, where the PDF import converts each page into drawing objects that can be edited. Images in the PDF, including images with a transparency mask, are converted along the way. An out-of-bounds write existed when an image with a transparency mask was converted, because positions taken from a crafted image were not checked against the size of the image buffer. In fixed versions the image size is limited, and the position of each mask pixel is checked before it is written.

LibreOffice Base documents can bind macros to document events, such as opening or closing the document. The macro security setting decides whether macros that come with a document may run. Macros bound to the events of a Base document were run without the macro security setting being applied, so opening or converting a crafted database document could run a macro and, through it, any command. In fixed versions macros bound to the events of a Base document follow the macro security setting, as macros in other documents do.

LibreOffice Writer can save documents in DOCX format. A document can contain content controls whose values are bound to custom XML data, and that data is updated with the current values when the document is exported, including in a conversion run from the command line. Values taken from the document were not escaped where they were used, so a crafted document could write a file of its choosing anywhere the user can write when it was exported to DOCX. In fixed versions these values are written into the document directly, and the XSLT transformations LibreOffice runs can no longer write files or use the network.

LibreOffice checks the digital signatures of a PDF document when the document is opened, and shows whether each signature is valid. An out-of-bounds write existed when a signature was checked, because the parts of the file that a crafted signature claims to cover were not checked against the size of the file. In fixed versions a signature that claims to cover anything outside the file is reported as not valid.

LibreOffice Calc can open spreadsheets in the DIF format, and text files such as CSV in the UTF-16 encoding. Both are read one line at a time. An out-of-bounds read existed when a line of a crafted file was read, because the length of the line could be miscalculated, so memory beyond the line could be copied into the imported document. In fixed versions each line is read up to its limit and no further.

LibreOffice Base documents can hold an embedded HSQLDB database. When the experimental features option is enabled, LibreOffice offers to migrate such a database to the embedded Firebird engine when the document is opened. A heap buffer overflow existed when binary values were copied during the migration, because a value could be longer than the space set aside for its column. In fixed versions that space is enlarged whenever a value is longer than its column.

LibreOffice can import documents in the HWP format, including pictures that link to an external file. An out-of-bounds read existed when the link target of a crafted picture was read, so memory past the picture data could end up in the converted document. In fixed versions the link target is taken only from the picture data.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 15.0.0 until 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, Next.js applications that use NextResponse to set cookies on Edge runtime routes expose the internal x-middleware-set-cookie header in the public response. This affects App Router route handlers and Pages Router Edge API routes. The header duplicates each cookie value and its attributes, so JavaScript already running on the same origin can read values that the Set-Cookie header marks HttpOnly, including sensitive session tokens set on an affected response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 15.0.0 until 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, the /_next/image optimizer in self-hosted Next.js deployments can process attacker-supplied SVG content even when dangerouslyAllowSVG is false, which is the default. The SVG reaches a parser that the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and vulnerabilities in SVG decoding. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. Prior to 15.5.29 and 16.4.5, self-hosted Next.js App Router route handlers and the fetch cache that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When the application is behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients. The resulting desynchronization can inject a response into another client's queue or disclose another client's response. This issue is fixed in versions 16.4.5 and 15.5.29.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.2.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications with Cache Components enabled can reuse an outer 'use cache' entry across root param values when a nested 'use cache' call reads a root param through next/root-params and returns a value containing pending promises. React Flight can deliver the ready portion to the outer function before the inner cache finishes publishing its root-param dependencies. The outer entry can then complete and be persisted under a key that omits the root param, causing the first written value to be served for other root param values and allowing the outer entry to ignore nested cache tag invalidation and lifetimes. The leaked value is not attacker controlled and depends on which invocation writes the entry first. This variant does not require an existing inner cache entry or a slow cache handler and is not covered by the fix for CVE-2026-103004. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. From 16.3.0 until 16.4.5, Next.js applications using the same 'use cache' function directly during rendering and through unstable_cache() can disclose cached data across root params when that function reads a root param. During the first fill after a cold process start, cross-request deduplication allows a concurrent unstable_cache() request to join the direct call's in-flight fill and receive its result before the root param mismatch is rejected. unstable_cache() then persists that result under a key that omits root params, causing later requests for other root param values to receive the same entry until revalidation or eviction. Exploitation requires the unstable_cache() request to arrive while the first fill is in flight. Outside this race, nesting 'use cache' inside unstable_cache() raises an unsupported-operation error, and avoiding that nesting prevents the issue. This issue is fixed in version 16.4.5.

In EDB Postgres Extended Server and EDB Postgres Advanced Server versions 15 through 18 with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled, the key used to encrypt temporary files was incompletely initialized. The code applied sizeof() to a pointer to the key buffer rather than to the buffer itself, so only 8 of the intended 32 bytes were filled from a secure random source and the remaining 24 bytes kept whatever was already in memory. This reduces the guaranteed randomness of the temporary-file key from 256 bits to 64 bits. Exploiting this requires local read access to the server's temporary-file directory, and those files normally exist only while the server is running; they persist only after a crash and are removed at the next server start. Permanent data files and WAL are not affected. The issue is fixed in EDB Postgres Extended Server 15.20, 16.16, 17.12 and 18.7 and EDB Postgres Advanced Server 15.20.0, 16.16.0, 17.12.0 and 18.7.0; the server must be restarted after upgrading.

qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.27, the privileged createFile helper followed attacker-controlled symbolic links during file creation. A local unprivileged user whose account is managed by the SSH Keys bundle could replace ~/.ssh with a link to /root/.ssh, causing the agent to write an authorized key for root. On systems using RAUC download mode with ineffective kernel symlink protection, the predictable /tmp/.bundle.raucb.part path could be linked to a system file and then overwritten or truncated during an update. A file-distribution destination beneath an attacker-controlled directory could similarly redirect the partial-download path so the agent changed ownership of a sensitive file. These vectors could result in root privilege escalation, arbitrary file modification, or denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 2026.27.

containerd is an open-source container runtime. From 2.2.0 until 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2, image manifest processing through the transfer service can encounter a child descriptor containing the io.containerd.manifest.subject annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image, including through a default CRI PullImage request, can trigger an unrecovered panic and crash the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes, kubelet retries can repeatedly trigger the crash and disrupt container operations on the worker node. This issue is fixed in versions 2.2.10, 2.3.7, and 2.4.2.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260428.0, the token GraphQL mutation used for primary login has no endpoint-specific rate limit, while the global Express limiter defaults to permitting 10,000 requests in a one-second window. An unauthenticated remote attacker can make password guesses at network speed against a chosen user account and, if a credential is recovered, access the account's threat-intelligence data and permitted operations. This issue is fixed in version 7.260428.0.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260722.0, the GraphQL endpoint accepts query operations over HTTP GET because CSRF prevention is disabled (csrfPrevention: false), placing the complete GraphQL query and its arguments in the request URL. Server and reverse-proxy logs, browser history, and shared caches can retain sensitive filters, marking-restricted identifiers, and investigation search arguments, allowing a person with access to those records to recover legitimate users' query contents. GraphQL mutations are not accepted over GET, and the issue does not permit code execution. This issue is fixed in version 7.260722.0.

GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. Prior to 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1, authenticated users can craft a URL that invokes massive actions without all required object- and action-specific authorization checks. The bypass permits operations outside the user's granted rights, including unauthorized plugin activation, deactivation, and uninstallation for plugins already present on the filesystem and other state-changing maintenance actions. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.28, 11.0.10, and 12.0.1.

GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. From 11.0.0 until 11.0.10 and 12.0.1, an authenticated technician can modify the two-factor authentication security of a user with higher privileges because the affected operations do not enforce all required authorization checks for the target user. This allows the technician to disable or take control of the higher-privileged user's two-factor authentication protection. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.10 and 12.0.1.

OpenCTI is an open source platform for managing cyber threat intelligence knowledge and observables. Prior to 7.260706.0, the logsWorkerConfig GraphQL query is authorized with the broad CONNECTORAPI capability and returns Elasticsearch connection details including elasticsearch_username, elasticsearch_password, elasticsearch_api_key, the URL, index, proxy, and TLS-verification setting. A holder of any connector API bearer token can retrieve this credential material. If the returned credentials are valid and Elasticsearch is reachable, the caller can directly read, modify, or delete OpenCTI indices and audit history outside application-layer role, marking, organization, and audit controls, with the practical impact bounded by the credentials' privileges and network reachability. This issue is fixed in version 7.260706.0.

Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in device certificate verification in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a TLS client certificate whose CA is not registered. When a client certificate chains to a root in the device endpoint's trust store but no CA in the chain is registered in NervesHub, NervesHub.SSL.decide/2 refuses it with the reason :unknown_ca. Erlang/OTP ssl reads that reason as a missing trust anchor, looks for an alternative root, finds the same root and validates again without end. The handshake process queries the database on each pass and keeps running after the client disconnects, until the node restarts.

The device endpoint trusts the public roots from CAStore unless DEVICE_SSL_CACERTFILE is set, so a client certificate from a public CA whose chain allows client authentication is sufficient. A chain that ends at a root outside the trust store is refused once.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.4.

An improper JWT signature verification vulnerability in CIRCUTOR PowerStudio SCADA WAVE desktop version allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authentication by submitting an unsigned JWT with the algorithm set to “none”. The shared JWT validation component accepts the token without verifying a cryptographic signature, allowing the attacker to impersonate another user and access protected functionality with that user's privileges.

In the Aliro access control reference
  applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
  Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA
  certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and
  the Aliro Step-up phase (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE) enabled,
  AccessManagerImpl::ProcessValidityIteration() treats a failed lookup of the
  Credential Issuer in the provisioned issuer array as success. For an issuer
  trusted through a certificate chain but not provisioned, the
  ValidityIteration (credential-rollback) check is therefore skipped. A former
  authorized holder with an old but correctly issuer-signed Access Document can
  be granted physical access after the issuer has advanced its iteration to
  revoke that credential. The default Matter provisioning configuration is not
  affected. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Aliro access control reference
  applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
  Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, the stored Access Document record does not
  retain validFrom and validUntil. The cached public key path (VerifyPublicKey())
  and the Kpersistent fast path (_VerifyKPersistentKey()) therefore never
  re-evaluate the Access Document validity period. An attacker who held a
  time-limited Aliro credential that was valid when first presented can
  continue to obtain physical access after the Access Document has expired, for
  as long as the cached record remains available. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In
the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door
Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with
CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the
1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a
0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in
place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This
resets that issuer's rollback protection. An attacker holding an older but correctly
signed Access Document from the adjacent issuer, whose validity iteration had
been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

In the Matter door lock applications of
  the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0
  through v1.1.1, AccessManager::ValidateCredential() checks only credential
  occupancy and the secret bytes, and never reads the owning user's UserStatus.
  It also returns success when no owning user can be resolved. A user suspended
  by setting their status to OccupiedDisabled can continue to unlock the door
  with their previously assigned credential, and an orphaned but occupied
  credential is also accepted. Fixed in v1.2.0.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the GET parameters `cod_primaria` and `cod_secundaria` of the Novanet Web endpoints `NNws_ShwNewDup` and `NPcd/NFG_VerNoticia`. User-provided data is reflected within a JavaScript block without proper sanitization or context-appropriate output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker could craft a manipulated URL that, when visited by a victim, would execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the victim’s browser, within the context of the affected site. The flaw resides in the platform’s shared code, so it could affect organizations using that vulnerable code.
